comments: A repeat of the 21 May 1982 show.
Only Tommy's show intro and outro are different to the original broadcast.

transcript.text: On 275 and 285, also in stereo on VHF, this is National Radio 1.
This is TV on the radio here, Thomas the Vance, and welcome to the Friday Rock Show.
Tonight, in the first Friday Rock Show of 1983, we repeat a major event of last year.
The first ever Royal Rock Show held at the NAC in Birmingham before His Royal Highness Prince Charles.
I don't know whether you read about it in the in the press or indeed saw it on television
But in the NEC, that's the National Exhibition Center in Birmingham within the arena known as the Birmingham International Arena
There was a magnificent event in rock. It was status quos 20th anniversary concert
The whole thing was put together for charity
It was to put together for the Prince's trust, which is a trust has been developed to help
disadvantaged and underprivileged kids in our country
I'd just like to say that, in my estimation,
it was probably the greatest event I'd ever been to.
The music was good, the atmosphere was absolutely electric.
To see 11,500 members of the Crow Army
all standing on their seats to welcome Prince Charles into the arena
and all shouting Charlie
gave me one of the biggest buzzes I think I've ever, ever experienced.
And that was how it sounded within the Birmingham International Arena.
Now, Prince Charles and the Palace gave permission for the national anthem
to be played by the band who were going to hit the stage.
This is Status Quo with our very own national anthem.
Just suppose an album again.
Hello.
I know you're a bit shocked that Don't Waste My Time came early,
but it's more of a shock.
So now it's singing time.
Anybody into it or what?
Everybody's going to offer a break.
So we try out then.
He said smiling sweetly at the crowd.
There's some stragglers at the front here, so the people at the back and the sides,
do you see me move to a gushto now?
Whoa!
We'll give him one more chance and see if we get a good...
It was also watched by countless thousands of people around the world on television.
The numbers that you heard were
Bye Bye Johnny, Down Down, Rain, Roadhouse Blues, Big Fat Mama,

4,500 times, Dirty Water, Don't Waste My Time, Over the Edge, Rockin' All Over the World, Hold Your Back, Whatever You Want, Don't Drive My Car, Little Lady, Backwater, Roll Over Lay Down, and Caroline.
And of course the band are Francis Rossi on vocals and guitars, Alan Lancaster on vocals and bass guitar, Rick Parfitt on lead guitar and rhythm guitar, he also does vocals too.
Andy Bowne on the keyboards, he's a vocalist as well,
and the drummer was the gentleman by the name of Pete Kershaw.
An exciting event, it really, really was.
And I must say that it raised something in excess of £50,000
for the Prince's Trust, going to go to help young people here in our country.
And that's it for this edition of the Friday Rock Show.
Next week, we are back to our normal pattern.
We'll have the first ever session by a group from Bristol, they're called Shiva.
